text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Amnesty International is concerned about cases of torture and mistreatment by police in Portugal, secretary-general Pierre Sane told the paper in an interview.
- Portuguese state airline TAP is negotiating to maintain planes of German airline Lufthansa.
- The next cabinet meeting on Thursday is expected to discuss the privatisation of tobacco company Tabaqueira.
- The cost of unemployment benefits to the social security department exceeded 350 billion escudos in 1995, according to a study by the communist-dominated CGTP trade union group.
- A new investment bank is expected to be set up in Guinea-Bissau next year.
- Portugal's second biggest pulp company Inapa will post 1996 profits of at least 800 million escudos, double the 1995 profit, Inapa's chairman Vasco Pessanha told the paper.
